column3: NASB supplies “there were.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“Jehohanan” is rendered “Johanan.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“For God had blessed him” is rendered “God had indeed blessed him.”
“The rulers” is rendered “who ruled over,” and “mighty men of ability” as “mighty men of valor.”
“His relatives, sons of ability” is rendered “whose brothers … were valiant men.”
The Hebrew reads sixty-two, as in NASB. “Man of ability” is rendered “able men.”
“Sons of ability” is rendered “valiant men.”
“The chief” is rendered “the first.”
Close to the Hebrew.
“To these belonged the divisions … duties” is rendered “To these divisions … were given duties.”
“For a gate and a gate” is rendered “for every gate.”
“East-ward” is rendered “to the east.” NASB supplies “for.”
“The house of the stores” is rendered “the storehouse”; NASB supplies “it fell” and “went.”
“Guard along side guard” is rendered “Guard corresponded to guard.” The name “Shuppim” may come from copying; the meaning is uncertain.
“To the day” is rendered “daily.”
The meaning of “Parbar” is uncertain; NASB keeps the word.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has the name “Ahijah”; NASB reads “their relatives,” as in the Greek. “Over the storehouses” is rendered “had charge of the treasures,” and “the holy things” as “the dedicated gifts.”
“Jehieli” is rendered “the Jehielites”; the Hebrew of this verse is awkward and its meaning is uncertain.
“Over the storehouses” is rendered “had charge of the treasures.”
NASB supplies “As for.”
“Chief” is rendered “officer,” and “storehouses” as “treasures.”
NASB reads “Shelomoth,” the spelling read aloud.
“Over the storehouses of the holy things” is rendered “had charge of all the treasures of the dedicated gifts.”
“Some of the wars and some of the plunder” is rendered “part of the spoil won in battles.”
NASB reads “Shelomoth,” the spelling read aloud. “On the hand of” is rendered “in the care of”; NASB supplies “anything” and “all of this.”
“The work outside” is rendered “outside duties”; NASB supplies “were assigned.”
“Oversight” is rendered “affairs.”
